x: The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other.
Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th.

It should also be recorded that other notabilities on this stage were Sando, Driver, Heatley, O'Gorman, Keily and Ingles, all of whom beat the previous record and all of whom gained assistance in battling with the opposition.

Steady as the pace was, the leaders were gradually dropping all sorts of big noises, but not our marathon novice Len, who had the "audacity" to lead at 13 miles and refused to drop a yard until 17 miles, when he lay 6th in the company of Hicks, Keily, Smith and Co.
